issues.body: The new text says the enumerated byte metrics are "the only hard-failing metrics." scripts/perf-gate.py instead classifies only mode=noise as advisory and puts every other regression in det_regs, which exits 2. bench/perf-baseline.json includes hard-failing non-byte mode=auto metrics, notably vectors_diskann_recall_at10, vectors_pq_recall_at10, and geo_compliance_deficit. Even the byte list is incomplete (for example comp_store_bytes_per_triple and fts_bytes_per_doc are mode=auto). The same inaccurate "only deterministic byte-count metrics hard-fail" formulation also appears in research/engine-performance-review.md and research/shacl-compact-and-shuttle-parsers-2026-07.md.
issues.fix_hint: Keep the accurate narrow statement that parse_ns_per_byte is advisory/non-blocking, but replace the exclusivity claim everywhere with wording such as: "mode=noise timing metrics are advisory; all mode=auto deterministic metrics hard-fail." Where metrics are listed, either make the list complete from bench/perf-baseline.json or clearly label it as examples/the metrics relevant to that proposal.
issues.title: The documents incorrectly say only byte-count metrics hard-fail

verdict.summary: The clarification that parse_ns_per_byte is advisory and non-blocking matches scripts/perf-gate.py. However, the new broader claim that only deterministic byte-count metrics hard-fail is false: the gate hard-fails every non-noise (deterministic) regression, including non-byte metrics such as vectors_diskann_recall_at10, vectors_pq_recall_at10, and geo_compliance_deficit. The documents also present an incomplete list of hard-gated byte metrics. Because this wording misstates the repository's merge gates in several audit/design records, it should be corrected before approval.
